messages:
Aisha Rahman: Heads-up: Product wants a minimal spec for tenant routing stability so we can include it in the long-term platform roadmap doc. Need launch gates + a pragmatic migration approach for multi-region tenants.
Ben Turner: +1. We should avoid full tenant slicing for V1. Propose a "preferred-region" mode with strict validation on fallbacks.
Claudia Park: Product constraints: opt-in only, clear billing impact, and must provide a simple customer consent flow. Also need CS to own communications for pilot customers.
Diego Morales: Infra notes: routing controller will keep a per-tenant affinity record (region, version, ttl). We'll need an atomic route-table rollout (vX) and a fast rollback mechanism. Also require fallback capacity checks before migrating a tenant.
Eli Ford: Telemetry we need pre-launch: p50/p95/p99 lat by tenant, fallback-hit-rate, cross-region egress (GiB) per-tenant, and reroute error count. Dashboards and an alerts playbook before canary.
Aisha Rahman: Suggested launch gates: 1) Canary: 1% traffic for 48h with p95 latency increase <=10% and error delta <=0.5pp. 2) Ramp: 10% for 24h, 50% for 6h, then full cutover. 3) Legal gate for data_residency=true tenants (signed doc).
Ben Turner: Implementation caveats: affinity TTL should be configurable per-tenant; default 24h. Migration needs a dry-run mode that updates affinity KV without changing traffic.
Claudia Park: I'll draft the opt-in form and a one-pager for customers outlining risks and rollback guarantees. Pricing note: run Sam's cost model to estimate the N+headroom delta.
Diego Morales: CLI examples for ops and devs:
```
# view tenant affinity
redwoodctl routing affinity get --tenant t_abc123 --env prod
# simulate migration (dry-run)
redwoodctl routing affinity set --tenant t_abc123 --region us-east-1 --dry-run
# force fallback
redwoodctl routing affinity set --tenant t_abc123 --region global-fallback --reason evacuate
```
Eli Ford: For the canary we need scriptable extraction of traces + tail logs for tenants. Also capturing KV-change events so telemetry and audit can be correlated.
Aisha Rahman: Action items: Claudia to own customer comms & opt-in draft (due Tue). Eli to own telemetry dashboard (due Wed). Diego to spike route-table rollout/rollback and dry-run tool (due Fri). Ben to draft canary SLA thresholds and emergency evacuation steps (due Fri).
Ben Turner: I'll add an emergency global-fallback command and make sure it can be invoked with RBAC and audit.
Claudia Park: Booked a 30m gating review next Thursday 11am PT. Will invite CS, legal, infra, and eng-sre.
ops-bot: Reminder created for 1781290000 to collect canary telemetry and route-controller logs.
Aisha Rahman: If we pass gates, add preferred-region routing to the Q3 roadmap as a low-risk initiative and schedule a 3-customer pilot.
